assertions.name: reproduces_all_three_ito_stated_floors
assertions.source: Includes the conjugation pair Ito uses to show the floor is not a conjugacy invariant -- the property this whole probe turns on.

assertions.name: positive_control_reaches_the_hypothesis
assertions.source: Delta^6 s1 s2^-1. Without this a null result elsewhere would be uninterpretable -- it could mean the search is broken.

assertions.name: search_raises_floors_by_conjugation
assertions.source: Ito's Delta^2 s2 s1^-1 has floor 0 as written and a floor-1 conjugate. Searching from the LOW side shows the search finds increases and does not merely re-report.

assertions.name: hyperbolic_figure_eight_never_meets_the_hypothesis
assertions.source: Searched 118097 conjugates in B_3. 4_1 IS hyperbolic (Vol 2.0299) and IS a knot, so Theorem 2 would apply to it if the floor condition could be met. A SEARCH result: no bound on the class supremum is computed.

description: Link-level successor to the Dehornoy floor probe: searches the conjugacy class (the Markov-I orbit, which is what the closure -- and hence Vol(K) -- actually depends on) for a representative meeting Ito's Theorem 2 hypothesis [beta]_D >= 3. A SEARCH over freely-reduced conjugators of length <= 10, not a proof: no bound on the supremum of the floor over a conjugacy class is computed or cited. Carries a positive control (a class that does reach 3) and a raising control (Ito's own pair, searched from the low side) so that a null result is readable as a fact about the class rather than about the search.

search_parameters.why_B_3: Ito states (s1 s2)^4 has floor 1 in B_3 and 0 in B_4: Delta_n^2 lengthens with n, the bracketing interval widens, and the floor can only fall. So the floor is maximised at minimal braid index and B_3 is the best case. This rests on that single stated example, not on a theorem verified here.

finding.claim: No sampled representative of the figure-eight knot's conjugacy class in B_3 reaches [beta]_D >= 3, so Ito's Theorem 2 cannot certify the hyperbolicity of 4_1 -- a knot that IS hyperbolic, with the volume the corpus's muon carrier uses.
finding.scope: (a) scope-limited negative: this construction, searched this far, does not meet the hypothesis. NOT (b): no invariant is proved to forbid it, and the supremum over the full conjugacy class is not computed.
finding.what_it_replaces: the word-level 'load-bearing' claim retracted in docs/audits/2026-08-25-ito-dehornoy-hyperbolicity-criterion.md, which read a floor off one chosen spelling as a fact about the link
finding.borromean_caveat: the Borromean row is a 3-COMPONENT LINK; Ito's Theorem 2 is stated for braids whose closure is a KNOT, so the theorem does not apply to it by hypothesis regardless of its floor. Reported for scale only.

corrects_a_sibling_conjecture.where: docs/audits/2026-08-25-atom-word-closures-are-not-hyperbolic.md, Addendum 2026-08-25, item 2 (landed on main as b437d3bb7e, and scoped by its author as a conjecture rather than a result)
corrects_a_sibling_conjecture.conjectured: small floor is 'precisely the regime where a word admits many closed-braid representatives and closures tend to be torus or composite'
corrects_a_sibling_conjecture.what_the_paper_states: the implication runs the other way. Ito Prop 4: non-braided satellite closure => [beta]_D < 3. Ito Remark 4, citing Menasco-Nakamura: composite closure => [beta]_D < 2. So composite => small floor.
corrects_a_sibling_conjecture.what_this_measurement_adds: the converse fails. 4_1 is PRIME and HYPERBOLIC and has floor 0 across 118097 conjugates. A small floor is a fact about SCALE, shared by hyperbolic and non-hyperbolic small links alike.
corrects_a_sibling_conjecture.what_is_NOT_affected: their primary conclusion. The atom words' non-hyperbolicity rests on monotonicity, which never touches the floor -- and Prop 4 read FORWARDS supports them: composite closures are exactly what must have small floor.

finding.not_computed: sup over the conjugacy class (Malyutin's quantity). That paper is not in library/; no bound from it is invoked here.
